sources.supports: latest interim revenue, profit and cash flow

sources.title: Data science and AI
sources.supports: AI capability and intended R&D uses

financial_anchor.caveat: FY2025 reported; H1 2026 reported operating profit was $7.410bn and must not be annualized.

ai_claim.claim: AstraZeneca uses AI in discovery and has named external discovery programmes.
ai_claim.limitation: No prospective matched evidence of improved stage-adjusted clinical success or retained cash found.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: Regulatory-quality validation remains required and candidate-generation speed is not clinical productivity.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Sector evidence, not an AstraZeneca failure study.

rights_limit: Patient, licensed real-world and collaboration data carry purpose- and contract-specific rights; public materials do not establish blanket cross-study training permission.
materiality_summary: Annual hurdle is $687m, 5% of FY2025 reported operating profit. A separate ten-year 10%-discounted equivalent is $4.22bn present value; discovery speed is not clinical success.

arithmetic.inputs: FY2025 reported operating profit $13.743bn; 10-year level contribution; 10% discount rate
arithmetic.result: $687m annual hurdle or $4.22bn same-duration PV equivalent; illustrative, not forecast.

g2_provisional: Open: scoped E1/E2 evidence, but no disclosed controlled clinical-productivity result or cash capture.
unresolved_questions: Which clinical programmes were prospectively AI-originated?
How do matched transition rates and total costs compare?
What cross-programme learning rights do collaborations permit?
